transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I... I suppose I came because I don’t feel much of anything good anymore. Even when my children are with me, or the sun’s out on the garden, it’s just... flat inside. Like that part of me has shut off.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About two weeks now… since my husband collapsed. The paramedics were there, in our kitchen, working on him. Since then, I think.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before your husband's collapse?

No… not really. The children come sit with me, and I try to feel comforted. I look out at the garden when the sun is on it. But it’s just… flat. Like the part of me that could feel glad about those things has gone quiet.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?
No… I can’t say there is. Even when the children sit with me, or I look at the garden in the sun, I just feel… flat. Like I should feel something, but I don’t.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your husband's collapse?
I… I don’t know. I keep turning it over, but I can’t really say. It’s all just… hard to think about.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself since your husband's collapse?
I… I don’t really want to talk about that. I don’t think so. It’s all just been… a lot.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your husband's collapse?
I’m… not really sure. I haven’t been paying much attention to that.
Have you been feeling restless or sluggish lately?
I’m not sure. I suppose I’ve just been… moving through the day as best I can. I haven’t really noticed if it’s restless or sluggish.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since your husband's collapse?
I… I can’t really say. Nights have been strange, but I haven’t kept track of whether I’m sleeping or not.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy before your husband's collapse that you still try to do, even if you don't find pleasure in them?

I still sit with my children when they come by, and I go out to the garden sometimes… but it doesn’t really reach me. Even with the sun there, I just feel sort of flat inside. Like I can’t feel glad or comforted the way I used to.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid much attention to how fast I’m moving… I just do what I have to do.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that about myself… I suppose I’m just getting through things.
Do you feel like your movements or reactions are slower than they should be?
I can’t really say. I haven’t noticed my movements being slower… I just feel like I’m doing things as they come.
Are there any activities you've stopped doing since your husband's collapse that you used to enjoy?

I used to go to the senior center… I don’t do that now. Mostly I just stay home. My daughter’s been helping with meals and errands and keeping track of things, because I don’t really manage it by myself lately. I don’t like being in the kitchen unless someone’s there with me.
Have you been having any thoughts about harming yourself since your husband's collapse?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I haven’t been thinking about that, I don’t think.
Do you feel like you have less energy than usual?
I don’t know… maybe. I’m tired a lot, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Do you feel like you're having trouble sitting still or that you're fidgeting more than usual?
I haven’t really noticed that. I mean… I don’t think I’m fidgeting. I mostly just sit.
Have you been having any thoughts of not wanting to live since your husband's collapse?
I… no, I don’t think so. I haven’t been thinking that way.
Have you had more than two weeks of feeling this way?
About two weeks… since he collapsed and the paramedics were there in the kitchen. It’s been like this since then.
